items.followUp: Explain molecular formula and give one example.

rubric.why: The simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms is the defining feature of an empirical formula.
rubric.description: Defines an empirical formula as showing the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms.

rubric.why: A correct example illustrates how an empirical formula represents the simplest ratio.
rubric.description: Gives glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆, with empirical formula CH₂O.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving glucose or its molecular formula together with its empirical formula.

modelAnswer: An empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element in a compound.
For example, glucose has the molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆; its empirical formula is CH₂O.

items.followUp: Define atomic radius and state the approximate atomic radius of oxygen.

rubric.why: Atomic radius is defined using half the distance between the nuclei of bonded atoms of the same element.
rubric.description: Defines atomic radius as half the distance between the nuclei of two bonded atoms of the same element.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the half-distance definition referring to nuclei of bonded atoms.

rubric.why: This is the approximate atomic radius of carbon.
rubric.description: States that carbon's atomic radius is approximately 77 pm (0.077 nm).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct approximate value with a unit.

modelAnswer: Atomic radius is half the distance between the nuclei of two bonded atoms of the same element.
The atomic radius of carbon is approximately 77 pm, or 0.077 nm.

items.followUp: Define electronegativity and describe its trend down a group.

rubric.why: Electronegativity describes an atom's attraction for the shared electrons in a molecule.
rubric.description: Defines electronegativity as the ability of an atom in a molecule to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining it in terms of attraction for shared or bonding electrons.

rubric.why: Electronegativity generally increases across a period from left to right.
rubric.description: States the trend in a period: electronegativity generally increases from left to right.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the correct direction of the trend across a period.

modelAnswer: Electronegativity is the ability of an atom in a molecule to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself.
Across a period, electronegativity generally increases from left to right.
